name: Visa de Residente (R) -- Estatuto Temporal de Protección para Migrantes Venezolanos (ETPV)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 continuous years holding a Special Permanence Permit (PEP), a Temporary Protection Permit (PPT), or a combination of both, without gaps in coverage.
requirements.fix_path: Accrue 5 continuous years under PEP and/or PPT status.

evidence_required.document: Documentation of continuous, uninterrupted PEP/PPT succession with no gaps
Migratory movement certificate covering the past 6 years
Criminal background record from country of origin
Proof of income/monthly amounts covering living expenses (may be requested at examiner's discretion)

outcome.duration_length: indefinite (renewal of the card itself requested every 5 years; automatically lapses after 2 consecutive years of absence from Colombia)

sources.title: Cancillería de Colombia -- Visa por aplicación del Estatuto Temporal de Protección para Migrantes Venezolanos: 5-year PEP/PPT requirement, application process, fees

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Colombia's initial build. Colombia's response to the Venezuelan displacement crisis (one of the largest in the Western Hemisphere) includes the ETPV/PPT framework registering over 2 million Venezuelan migrants -- this route models the RESIDENT-VISA end of that pipeline (5 years of PEP/PPT time converting to an R visa), confirmed directly at tier-1 including fees (~USD 455 Americas/global, ~EUR 177 Europe/Cuba). The earlier-stage Temporary Protection Permit (PPT) itself -- the initial humanitarian registration that most Venezuelan migrants actually hold day-to-day, which grants work rights and regularization without yet reaching this 5-year R-visa threshold -- was NOT independently researched and sourced as its own route in this pass; it is arguably the more commonly used and more humanitarian-flavoured status, and is flagged here as a gap for a future revisit rather than assumed to be adequately covered by this R-visa route alone. Category set to 'settled' (not 'humanitarian') since this specific route's documented content is about the residency/settlement outcome, not the initial protection determination.
